source.title: ANF03. Latin Christianity: Its Founder, Tertullian
ANF03. Latin Christianity: Its Founder, Tertullian

verses.text: But how gracefully has the Divine Wisdom arranged the order of the prayer; so that after things heavenly—that is, after the “Name” of God, the “Will” of God, and the “Kingdom” of God—it should give earthly necessities also room for a petition!
verses.modernizedText: But how gracefully has the Divine Wisdom arranged the order of the prayer; so that after things heavenly—that is, after the “Name” of God, the “Will” of God, and the “Kingdom” of God—it should give earthly necessities also room for a petition!

verses.text: For the Lord had withal issued His edict, “Seek ye first the kingdom, and then even these shall be added:” albeit we may rather understand, “Give us this day our daily bread,” spiritually.
verses.modernizedText: For the Lord had also issued His edict, “Seek ye first the kingdom, and then even these shall be added:” although we may rather understand, “Give us this day our daily bread,” spiritually.

verses.text: For Christ is our Bread; because Christ is Life, and bread is life.
verses.modernizedText: For Christ is our Bread; because Christ is Life, and bread is life.

verses.text: “I am,” saith He, “the Bread of Life;” and, a little above, “The Bread is the Word of the living God, who came down from the heavens.”
verses.modernizedText: “I am,” He says, “the Bread of Life;” and, a little above, “The Bread is the Word of the living God, who came down from the heavens.”

verses.text: Then we find, too, that His body is reckoned in bread: “This is my body.”
verses.modernizedText: Then we find, too, that His body is reckoned in bread: “This is my body.”

verses.text: And so, in petitioning for “daily bread,” we ask for perpetuity in Christ, and indivisibility from His body.
verses.modernizedText: And so, in petitioning for “daily bread,” we ask for continuance in Christ and inseparability from His body.

verses.text: But, because that word is admissible in a carnal sense too, it cannot be so used without the religious remembrance withal of spiritual Discipline; for (the Lord) commands that bread be prayed for, which is the only food necessary for believers; for “all other things the nations seek after.”
verses.modernizedText: But, because that word is also capable of a bodily meaning, it cannot be so used without also remembering spiritual Discipline in a religious spirit; for (the Lord) commands that bread be prayed for, which is the only food necessary for believers; for “all other things the nations seek after.”

verses.text: The like lesson He both inculcates by examples, and repeatedly handles in parables, when He says, “Doth a father take away bread from his children, and hand it to dogs?” and again, “Doth a father give his son a stone when he asks for bread?”
verses.modernizedText: He teaches the same lesson by examples and repeatedly treats it in parables, when He says, “Doth a father take away bread from his children, and hand it to dogs?” and again, “Doth a father give his son a stone when he asks for bread?”

verses.text: For He thus shows what it is that sons expect from their father.
verses.modernizedText: For He thus shows what it is that sons expect from their father.

verses.text: Nay, even that nocturnal knocker knocked for “bread.”
verses.modernizedText: Nay, even the one who knocked at night knocked for “bread.”

verses.text: Moreover, He justly added, “Give us this day,” seeing He had previously said, “Take no careful thought about the morrow, what ye are to eat.”
verses.modernizedText: Moreover, He justly added, “Give us this day,” seeing He had previously said, “Take no careful thought about the morrow, what ye are to eat.”

verses.text: To which subject He also adapted the parable of the man who pondered on an enlargement of his barns for his forthcoming fruits, and on seasons of prolonged security; but that very night he dies.
verses.modernizedText: To which subject He also adapted the parable of the man who pondered on an enlargement of his barns for his coming harvest, and on seasons of prolonged security; but that very night he dies.
